answer: Require each agent to lock a nontransferable bond before it can sell work in the harbor. A validator checks the signed task receipt, samples the underlying evidence, and slashes the bond when the same result is submitted under multiple keys or a forged source is proven. A marble seal can bind the receipt to one epoch, while nectar marks a single consumed claim. Creating n aliases therefore requires n locked bonds and n independently verifiable jobs; copying keys adds liability but no reward.
